subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw's native backup CLI add gitignore-style exclusions now, and what default, protected-path, ignore-file, and manifest rules are acceptable for restore-critical and sensitive data?
rationale: This changes a core recovery and security command, and the active implementation candidate raises choices around smart defaults, protected paths, auto-loaded ignore files, manifest contents, dependency scope, and proof that automation should not settle for maintainers.

options.title: Narrow and review native excludes
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow the active implementation into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Keep the issue as product backlog and direct users to Keep My Claw or manual cleanup until maintainers are ready to own the native CLI surface.

options.title: Reject native backup filtering
options.body: Close only after documenting the supported plugin or ClawHub alternative and the security tradeoffs of not adding native fine-grained filtering.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review native excludes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask maintainers to narrow the active implementation into an opt-in, proof-backed design with explicit protected restore paths and no silent backup-scope changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the touched backup files makes this the best available routing candidate for the product/security decision, with original backup authors as supporting context.
